title: Fintech & Architecture Briefing — Thursday 26 Nov 2026
note: Thursday edition covering 23–25 Nov; nothing from issue 5 is repeated. Two catch-ups that no earlier issue covered are included because they are material: Java4Shell (17 Nov) and Eurobank–Fibank (18–19 Nov). I ran 24 searches. ECB, EBA, InfoQ, CNCF, Confluent and the Medium feeds were fetched directly. Finextra, BleepingComputer and the Bank of Greece returned 403, and fintechfutures.com and retailbankerinternational.com are blocked by this session's network policy, so the two catch-ups rest on search summaries. Medium summaries come from feed previews only, because story pages returned 403. Sections 5–7 were quiet. Merged 22 overlapping posts into 4 items. The November Software Architects' Newsletter is due 27 Nov and will be covered on Monday. The Docs type needs a connector that is not attached, so the editable copy is an HTML page. No Projects tool was available, so the Projects copy and the backfill check were skipped.

sixty.t: Catch-up: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938, CVSS 9.2) can corrupt the heap through the HotSpot JVM's Base64 decoder on Java 17, 21, 25 and 27. Patch TIBCO, Kafka, Keycloak, Jenkins and AKS images, or use -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as a stopgap.
ECB: DLT-issued assets reaching T2S through eligible CSD links become Eurosystem collateral from June 2027, with detailed rules due in spring 2027.
ECB SPACE 2026: cards (45%) overtook cash (44%) in shops for the first time, and mobile payments reached 9%.
Sweden will move krona RTGS settlement to T2 by February 2030, which makes T2 a three-currency platform.
InfoQ pick: a blueprint for AI-drafted suspicious activity reports (grounded claims, judge plus fact-checker, golden-set release gates). A ready template for our financial-crime GenAI pilot.
InfoQ (QCon SF): treat AI agents as an insider risk. Give them their own principals, attenuated tokens and an egress proxy that swaps in real keys.

sections.title: European regulation & supervision
sections.quiet: There were no new DORA, PSD3/PSR, FiDA, AMLA or AI Act texts. The EBA issued a hotfix for reporting framework v4.4 Phase 1 (25 Nov), which our regulatory-reporting team should apply.

items.h: EBA report: stablecoins, including MiCA e-money tokens, are central to DeFi
items.s: The EBA finds that stablecoins, including some MiCA e-money tokens, provide most of DeFi's liquidity, collateral and settlement. It warns that this can pass risk back to issuers and to the CASPs that act as gateways, and that DeFi structures can be used to get around MiCA's ban on paying interest on EMTs. The EBA again asks the Commission to consider extra rules for CASPs offering DeFi lending access, as part of the MiCA review.
items.w: If we issue, distribute or custody EMTs, expect DeFi-exposure controls to come out of the MiCA review. Wallet and transaction monitoring should be able to flag flows to DeFi protocols.

sections.title: Payments
sections.quiet: There was no digital euro trilogue news and no TIPS, SEPA Inst, Wero or EPC releases in the window. Swift's new CBPR+ timeline for structured addresses is still due by December.

items.h: ECB: DLT-issued assets can be pledged as Eurosystem collateral from June 2027
items.s: Assets issued on DLT platforms licensed under the DLT Pilot Regime become eligible collateral if they reach T2S through an eligible CSD link and meet extra conditions on settlement finality and outsourcing. Detailed requirements are due in spring 2027, with go-live in June 2027. The ECB presents this as a step towards a tokenised collateral framework.
items.w: ECMS connectivity, the securities master on IBM i and the custody feeds will need to handle DLT-issued ISINs. Put tokenised collateral on the 2027 target architecture and ask Treasury about Pilot Regime issuances in its pipeline.

items.h: ECB SPACE 2026: cards overtake cash at the point of sale for the first time
items.s: Cards made up 45% of in-store transactions by number, against 44% for cash, the first time cards have led since the series began in 2016. Mobile payments reached 9%, up from 6%. In every euro-area country at least 12% of consumers had a card or mobile payment refused in the previous month. The release gives no Greek figures.
items.w: This supports investment in mobile wallets, IRIS and SoftPOS, and in capacity for card authorisation. Ask the payments analysts to pull the Greek annex from the full report.

items.h: Sweden signs up to join T2 for krona large-value payments, with migration targeted for February 2030
items.s: The ECB and the Riksbank signed an agreement to move Swedish krona RTGS settlement to T2, with migration targeted for February 2030. T2 already settles Danish krone, and Sweden already uses TIPS.
items.w: Nothing changes for us directly. It strengthens the case for building our payment hub's RTGS and instant adapters on Eurosystem ISO 20022 standards rather than national variants.

sections.title: Greece
sections.quiet: No Bank of Greece, HBA or DIAS/IRIS technology news for 23–25 Nov. Morgan Stanley rated Eurobank, Alpha and Piraeus Overweight on 24 Nov.

items.h: Catch-up: Eurobank agrees to buy 65% of Bulgaria's Fibank for €650m
items.s: Eurobank agreed to buy a 65% stake in Bulgaria's First Investment Bank (Fibank) for about €650m, partly funded by a planned €750m capital increase. No earlier issue covered the deal, and this summary rests on syndicated trade press.
items.w: Peers are buying scale in South-East Europe, which brings multi-entity core and payment integration and DORA registers that must absorb acquired entities' contracts. A reusable integration playbook (canonical model, TIBCO/Kafka layer per entity, decision on core consolidation) belongs on the SAB shelf.

sections.title: Payment & banking security
sections.quiet: The n0n vendor breach (issues 3 and 5) produced no new confirmed facts. One threat-research write-up blames compromised credentials at the analytics vendor Qubole, which the banks have not confirmed.

items.h: Catch-up: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a pre-auth heap corruption in the HotSpot JVM's Base64 decoder
items.s: CVE-2026-114938 is a heap out-of-bounds write in the HotSpot JVM's x86-64 Base64 intrinsic. It can be reached on AVX-512 VBMI CPUs, which covers most current server generations, and researchers showed pre-auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins and Keycloak. Java 17 (from 17.0.6), 21, 25 and 27 are affected, while Java 8 and 11 are not listed. CVSS 4.0 is 9.2. Oracle and OpenJDK patched on 17 Nov and CISA urged immediate patching. There was no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation as of 18 Nov, but opportunistic probing has been reported. The stopgap is to restart JVMs with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics.
items.w: Our exposure is TIBCO BW/EMS, Kafka brokers and Connect, Keycloak, Jenkins and Spring on AKS, mostly running on AVX-512 Azure SKUs. Rebuild base images and use the flag where patching has to wait. IBM i Java runs on J9 rather than HotSpot, so it is probably out of scope, but get confirmation from IBM. Collect TIBCO, Confluent and Databricks bulletins as DORA evidence.

sections.title: Solution architecture & backend
sections.quiet: Nothing material came from Confluent, the CNCF, Azure, Databricks, TIBCO or IBM on 23–25 Nov. This week's architecture substance is in section 8.

sections.title: Enterprise AI in banking
sections.quiet: There were no new European bank GenAI deployments and no EBA, ECB, BIS or FSB AI guidance. See the InfoQ SAR blueprint in section 8.

sections.title: Industry moves
sections.quiet: No material core-banking or European fintech deals. Taxfix bought Countingup (24 Nov), and TPG and Corpay agreed to take BILL private (23 Nov).

items.h: AI architecture: evals, grounding and release gates for AI-drafted suspicious activity reports
items.s: A reference design for drafting suspicious activity reports with a multi-agent pipeline. Every claim is grounded with a source ID, and a judge model plus a deterministic fact-checker gate publication. A golden dataset gates every prompt or model change, and releases need compliance, risk and legal sign-off before shadow and canary rollout. When evidence is missing the agent returns 'insufficient context' instead of guessing.
items.w: This is close to a ready-made template for our financial-crime GenAI pilot on Azure OpenAI and Databricks. Treat prompts and models as regulated changes under model risk management, and freeze the judge model's version.

items.h: AI architecture: securing AI agents as an insider-risk problem (QCon SF)
items.s: Google's Amanda Walker argues that agents need their own principals, because an agent holding a user's authority can be turned against that user through prompt injection. She recommends attenuated tokens minted per sub-agent, Biscuit-style tokens that can only be narrowed, and an egress proxy that swaps short-lived synthetic keys for real ones. Containment comes from sandboxes and sidecar policy over what an agent can call.
items.w: This fits Entra Agent ID and the AKS Agent Sandbox (issue 4). Make agent principals, attenuated tokens and an APIM egress proxy mandatory in our agent harness standard.

items.h: Architecture & Design: CNCF research finds VMs still host 53% of production apps
items.s: A CNCF and Linux Foundation survey of 492 organisations finds that VMs host 53% of production apps on average, and 64% at large enterprises. 71% expect that share to stay flat. Where VM use is growing, the reasons are isolation (47%) and AI or agent workloads (34%). MicroVM sandboxing and confidential computing are the expected growth areas.
items.w: This supports a hybrid AKS, VM and IBM i platform strategy rather than a containers-only target.

items.h: Architecture & Design: DoorDash splits coordination from computation and scales dispatch 10x
items.s: DoorDash split dispatch into a stateful coordinator that owns lifecycle, state and rules, and stateless workers that run optimisation and inference on sharded data over gRPC. The result was 10x throughput and availability above 99.99% at peak.
items.w: The same split suits fraud scoring and payment routing: one owner for state, stateless scoring scaled out on AKS, and a clean failure boundary for DORA scenario tests.

items.h: Dual Writes Will Eventually Corrupt Your Data: How We Migrated to the Transactional Outbox Pattern — Sonam Patel (tag: kafka)
items.s: A production write-up that starts from 1,284 orders sitting in Postgres that no downstream service ever received, the classic dual-write failure. It describes the migration to a transactional outbox (summary from the feed preview).
items.w: We carry the same risk wherever an AKS service or TIBCO process writes to a database and publishes to Kafka in two steps. Outbox plus CDC should be the default in our event-driven integration standard.

items.h: Your Azure MCP is only as safe as the identity it runs with — Part 1 — Camilla Santoro (tag: azure)
items.s: Many teams run the Azure MCP Server under their own admin identity, so every misunderstood prompt runs with admin rights. Part 1 argues for a dedicated, least-privilege identity (summary from the feed preview).
items.w: Require managed identities with scoped RBAC and read-only defaults before the platform team adopts Azure MCP.

items.h: Why FAPI 2.0 and DPoP Are the Future of Corporate Open Banking — Davide V. (tag: open-banking)
items.s: The article argues for moving B2B banking API security from mTLS to application-layer cryptography under FAPI 2.0, using private_key_jwt client authentication (RFC 7523) and DPoP sender-constrained tokens (RFC 9449) (summary from the feed preview).
items.w: This matters for the APIM roadmap for corporate and PSD3/PSR APIs. DPoP survives proxies and gateways that break mTLS binding, so assess FAPI 2.0 support in APIM and our identity provider.

agenda.p: Confirm patch status for TIBCO, Kafka, Keycloak, Jenkins and the AKS base images, and get written statements from IBM, TIBCO, Confluent and Databricks. Check that our SBOM tooling can say which JVM builds run where within hours.

agenda.b: GenAI in financial crime: adopt a reference pattern.
agenda.p: Adopt the InfoQ SAR blueprint as the SAB standard for any GenAI that drafts regulated output, and name who signs off prompt and model changes.
Check that ECMS, the securities master and the T2S/CSD interfaces can carry DLT-issued assets before the June 2027 go-live.
Make agent principals (Entra Agent ID or managed identities), attenuated tokens and an APIM egress proxy mandatory, starting with Azure MCP and coding agents.
